explanation: The feature gives the brook a course, and a course costs. MEASURED ALTERNATELY against a detached worktree at the pre-feature commit, three rounds each interleaved so the same machine load fell on both (the GM asked whether the box was simply busy with other sessions; it was not): baseline 27.9 / 28.3 / 28.4 s against 35.6 / 36.3 s. The newest bookend pair reads +21.9% total. TWO CAUSES, both diagnosed. (1) The FIELD stage, which is seeds 25 and 39: cutting the fan's canal away from the brook removes about a seventh of its area, so the acreage search's own ceiling comes down and seeds near it SATURATE at every aspect - 15 carves on cohort seed 25 against 3 before the feature. The arithmetic fix is exact and was measured at -3.6%, and it is NOT taken: it changes the size every fan is fitted at, and the gate measured what that costs at the fan's toe - one basin of 618 tapering below the 15 degree needle bar, and no flooded plot painted at all on the reference roll, so the sheet loses the wet-paddy class it exists to exhibit. The comment at the point of change carries both numbers and names the toe as what a later feature must fix first. (2) The WEB and TRACK stages, which is seeds 4 and 47: the brook is a watercourse the lane router must now avoid along the whole map rather than a stub at the field's head, and on seeds whose cluster the new seat rule moved the web lays more links. Measured under cProfile on the reference seed: web 1.58s to 6.19s, _route 35 calls to 66, fouled() 80,265 to 472,244 - all of them through the existing PointGrid and edge_within indexes, so this is more work of the same shape rather than a scan that should have been indexed (constitution X clause 15). Nothing here is a per-candidate scan of geometry that does not change during the scan.
